extra.message: Chat message content received over an untrusted WebSocket (chatMessage.author.name and chatMessage.message, parsed from STOMP message body at line 49) is concatenated directly into an HTML string and assigned to element.innerHTML. Any other authenticated user can send arbitrary text via sendChatToBackend(), which is echoed back through this socket and rendered as raw HTML, allowing stored/DOM-based XSS (e.g. a chat message containing ``).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: user.emailAddress (free-text, attacker-controllable at registration via Register.js, unvalidated) is passed to jQuery's .replaceWith(). jQuery treats a string argument as HTML markup, so an email address value such as '' is parsed and executed as HTML/JS in the victim's browser when another user views the contact list, resulting in stored DOM XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: user.webPageUrl is set as an unvalidated free-text field during registration (Register.js line 70, no URL/protocol validation) and later rendered directly as the href of an anchor tag. A registered user can set webPageUrl to a `javascript:` URI (e.g. `javascript:alert(document.cookie)`), which executes when another logged-in user clicks 'Go to <name>s web page' in the profile popup.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Anchor tag uses target="_blank" with an attacker-influenced href (user.webPageUrl) but no rel="noopener noreferrer". The linked page can access window.opener and redirect the original SoCinema tab to a phishing page (reverse tabnabbing).

cwe: CWE-1022: Use of Web Link to Untrusted Target with window.opener Access

extra.message: Hardcoded credentials ('asdf', 'were') are used to authenticate the STOMP client.connect() call to the WebSocket notification channel, for every user session.

Backend base URLs are hardcoded as plain http:// (not https://). Login.js posts username/password and Register.js posts the full registration form (including password) to these endpoints, so credentials and session cookies are transmitted in cleartext over the network.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The full JSON login response from the backend is stored verbatim in window.localStorage (loggedInUser), and a plain 'loggedIn' flag is also stored (App.js lines 38-39). localStorage is readable by any script running on the origin (e.g. via the stored XSS in Users.js) and persists across sessions/tabs, unlike an HttpOnly cookie, exposing any tokens/session data included in the login response to theft.

cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information

extra.message: Routes for /users, /profile, and /messages are registered without any authentication guard/onEnter check. Access control is implemented only by conditionally hiding nav links in App.js based on client-side state (this.state.loggedIn), which is trivially bypassed by navigating directly to the URL (e.g. typing /users in the address bar) even when not logged in, relying entirely on the backend to reject the resulting API calls.
